s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and abdominal pain in the context of fasting and marked weight loss
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Abdominal ultrasonography showed marked gastric distension
Plain radiographs showed marked gastric distension
Nasogastric tube was placed for decompression
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum
No intrinsic luminal lesions found on endoscopy

shortlist.label: Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, consistent with patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Gastric Outlet Obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Marked gastric distension and vomiting, with normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, suggesting a mechanical obstruction

shortlist.label: Gastroparesis
shortlist.why_kept: Intractable vomiting, bloating, and progressive inability to tolerate oral intake, consistent with delayed gastric emptying

shortlist.label: Small Bowel Obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Postprandial upper abdominal pain, vomiting, and bloating, with imaging findings suggestive of mechanical obstruction

shortlist.label: Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the duodenum and symptoms consistent with intermittent obstruction, although less likely than Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome

raw.rationale: The contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, which is a hallmark of Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome, especially in the context of marked leanness and recent fasting which could exacerbate the condition.

rejected.label: Gastric Outlet Obstruction
rejected.why: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal, with no intrinsic luminal lesions found, making an intrinsic obstruction less likely.

rejected.label: Gastroparesis
rejected.why: While gastroparesis could explain some symptoms, the specific finding of duodenal compression on CT points more directly to a mechanical issue like Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome.

rejected.label: Small Bowel Obstruction
rejected.why: The absence of intrinsic luminal lesions and the specific location of the compression (third portion of the duodenum) make Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome a more precise diagnosis than a general small bowel obstruction.

rejected.label: Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves compression of the celiac artery, not the duodenum, which was the specific site of compression in this case, making Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome a better fit for the symptoms and findings described.
